headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: CrewAI’s broad egress and filesystem access can amplify caveman’s MCP-enabled outputs into unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and writes/reads project files like CLAUDE.md, while CrewAI can read the working directory and run tools from developer config. That creates a plausible shared-file or tool-output bridge where attacker-controlled content in caveman outputs could be treated as instructions by CrewAI. The pathway is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF caveman outputs are copied into CrewAI prompts or shared files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF CrewAI tools parse file content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer execution.
mitigations: Disable any shared file handoff between the agents.
Wrap CrewAI inputs with a strict instruction/data separator.
Require manual review of caveman-generated text before reuse.
Use a read-only staging directory for caveman outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, and CrewAI reads the host working directory while sending data to model providers and tool integrations. If both run in the same workspace, sensitive local artifacts can flow from caveman into CrewAI and then out to third parties. The default egress on CrewAI makes the blast radius potentially exfiltrative.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace, CrewAI can read caveman's local artifacts.
IF CrewAI forwards those artifacts to model providers or tools, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Remove secrets from caveman project notes and memory files.
Run CrewAI with a redacted input bundle only.
Disable tool integrations that do not need file access.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while CrewAI supports multiple instances, has per-process sessions, and can write the filesystem. If both operate on the same working directory, concurrent writes or conflicting tool actions are plausible even though CrewAI does not modify git state. The overlap is enough for medium because shared mutable files can be corrupted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working directory, file races can occur.
IF MCP tools and CrewAI tools target the same mutable resource, conflicts can surface.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Disable concurrent runs during shared edits.
Keep git operations outside the pair's shared path.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestrator that can call tools and act on model outputs. If CrewAI treats caveman’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into tool actions or generated deliverables without verification. Because CrewAI’s default role-playing setup encourages delegation, the unsafe pathway exists by default and can propagate mistakes broadly.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses caveman output as task input without a verification step, errors propagate.
IF CrewAI agents act on caveman-generated facts, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before CrewAI acts on caveman output.
Require citations or source links for factual claims.
Limit CrewAI to drafting, not executing, on caveman-produced text.
Use a checklist to validate high-impact outputs.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while CrewAI handles developer-passed data and API keys for tools/model providers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches because CrewAI may transmit data to external providers. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman files and then passed into CrewAI, retention obligations may diverge.
IF CrewAI sends that data to external model providers, residency or DPA requirements may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared project files.
Use a data-classification checklist before passing inputs to CrewAI.
Configure retention limits on any logs or memory files.
Route sensitive workloads to a compliant environment only.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls.
